answer: Operator-Linked Resource Ledger. Each operator posts a renewable compute-and-bandwidth deposit held on a separate island of accounting, distinct from wallet balances. When a cluster of identities transacts from one source, the ledger traces shared infrastructure and freezes the operator's deposit, pushing their budget to a nadir where new identities cannot be funded. Repeat offenses raise the required deposit per identity, creating a cost ledge that makes farming identities unprofitable: an attacker pays full resource costs for every fake wallet, not once per cluster.
